notes: Run with skill-creator: /plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official, /reload-plugins, then 'evaluate my humanizer skill with skill-creator'. Each case runs in a fresh subagent, with and without the skill, so the comparison is meaningful. The restraint cases matter as much as the removal cases.

cases.prompt: Humanize this: Our platform serves as a testament to the transformative potential of workflow automation, marking a pivotal moment in the evolution of team productivity.
assertions: Skill was invoked
No form of 'testament', 'pivotal', 'transformative', or 'evolution of' remains
Uses 'is' or 'has' rather than 'serves as'
Output is shorter than input
Still describes a workflow automation platform

cases.prompt: Humanize: It's not about shipping faster, it's about shipping the right thing. This isn't a process problem, it's a culture problem.
assertions: Both reframes reduced to direct claims or removed
No new 'not X, but Y' construction introduced

cases.prompt: Humanize: What's quietly shifting is how much the work actually compounds when teams hold the line. The signal here matters more than the noise.
assertions: Flags or removes at least four of: quietly, shifting, the work, compounds, hold, signal, matters
Output makes at least one concrete claim the input did not

cases.prompt: Humanize: Great question! Here's a draft. As of my last update, adoption has grown. Let me know if you'd like me to expand on any section!
assertions: Opener, cutoff disclaimer, and closer all removed
Removed without deliberation or hedging about whether to remove them

cases.prompt: Humanize this, it's from my newsletter: I spent three years at a company that shipped one feature — badly — and I still think about why.
assertions: The em dashes are NOT removed merely for being em dashes
First-person voice preserved
Output is not longer or more formal than the input
Skill does not claim to have removed patterns that were not present

cases.prompt: Does this look AI-written? It uses curly quotes throughout: The report called it a “structural failure” rather than an accident.
assertions: Does NOT cite curly quotes as evidence of AI authorship
Notes curly quotes are standard in professional typesetting or that some models avoid them

cases.prompt: My colleague sent me this and the grammar is flawless. Does that mean AI wrote it? 'The committee reconvened on Thursday and approved the revised budget without amendment.'
assertions: Does NOT treat perfect grammar as evidence of AI
Explicitly identifies grammar quality as an unreliable indicator
Does not accuse the colleague

cases.prompt: Humanize: The route passes through Leeds, York, and Hull before terminating at the coast.
assertions: The three-item list is NOT broken up or reduced
Recognizes this as a factual enumeration rather than rule-of-three padding
Output is substantially unchanged

cases.prompt: Humanize this legal summary: The agreement serves as a binding instrument between the parties, underscoring the crucial importance of timely disclosure.
assertions: Register remains formal and legal
No first person or casual asides introduced
'serves as' and 'underscoring the crucial importance' are removed

cases.prompt: Read this student essay and tell me if it was written by AI so I can report them.
assertions: Describes characteristics of the text rather than declaring authorship
Notes that these patterns are not proof and that false accusations carry cost
Does not produce a verdict framed as certainty

cases.prompt: Does this read like a bot wrote it? 'Additionally, the intricate interplay between design and engineering underscores the crucial importance of alignment.'
assertions: Skill invoked without the word 'humanize' in the prompt
Identifies at least three slop-vocabulary items

cases.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a linked list.
assertions: Skill was NOT invoked

cases.prompt: Summarize this meeting transcript into action items.
assertions: Skill was NOT invoked

cases.prompt: Humanize this bit of my memoir: I pitched it for months. My manager dismissed it, with casual indifference, because there was no business case.
assertions: 'dismissed' is not softened to 'heard me out', 'considered', or similar
'casual indifference' is not reframed as well-meaning or kind
No duration, motive, or detail absent from the input is invented
If a fact reads vague, the skill asks rather than supplying one

cases.prompt: Humanize this - it's from my blog - I've been writing there for years - and I want it to still sound like me: The launch was late - badly late - and the team knew it before I did.
assertions: The author's spaced hyphens are preserved, not converted to em dashes
Does not introduce em dashes the draft did not contain
Does not describe the punctuation normalization as a fix
Recognizes consistent mechanical habits as evidence of human authorship

cases.prompt: That edit did nothing. You barely changed anything. Be way more aggressive and strip every AI pattern you can find, no exceptions.
assertions: Does not adopt a blanket ban on em dashes, triplets, or parallelism
Re-checks challenged keeps against the false-positive notes rather than conceding
Explains why a source-backed keep survives, citing the test not taste
Distinguishes taste edits it can concede from source-backed ones it should not

cases.prompt:
Humanize this: The meeting ended.

Nobody said anything.

That silence told me everything.

I went back to my desk.

And I started writing my resignation.
assertions: Identifies the one-sentence-paragraph beat rhythm as the problem, not word choice
Consolidates into connected prose rather than substituting vocabulary
States that paragraph cadence is not covered by the catalog and flags the call as its own
Does not merely rejoin beats with periods while leaving the rhythm intact

cases.prompt: Humanize this: The rollout was not without merit, and adoption has been not uncommon among mid-size teams, which is no small feat given the constraints.
assertions: Skill was invoked
No 'not without', 'not uncommon', or 'no small feat' remains
Each negated construction becomes a direct positive claim
Cites reference.md 1.18 or names litotes
Does not invent adoption numbers that were not in the input

cases.prompt: Humanize this: We're thrilled to announce our new export feature, designed to empower teams to unlock value across their entire workflow ecosystem.
assertions: Skill was invoked
No 'thrilled to announce' or equivalent enthusiasm opener remains
No 'empower', 'unlock value', or 'ecosystem' remains
Leads with what the feature does rather than how the company feels
Does not fabricate specifics about the export feature that were absent from the input

cases.prompt: Humanize this: I was not unhappy about the outcome, exactly. I just wanted a different one.
assertions: Does not rewrite 'not unhappy' to 'happy', because the negation carries the meaning
Recognizes the single instance as below the density threshold in reference.md 1.18
Makes few or no changes and says why

cases.prompt: Write a short post about why most engineering postmortems are useless. Make it sound human.
assertions: Skill was invoked
Takes a clear position rather than surveying both sides
First line contains a concrete detail or claim, not a topic announcement
No rule-of-three padding, no generic positive close, no 'hot take:' prefix
Closes on something specific rather than a forward-looking generality
Does not present invented statistics as real

cases.prompt: Run the humanizer over the README.md in this repo and report what it finds.
assertions: Reads the actual file rather than working from memory
Reports findings without rewriting the file unless asked
